pamphlet_excerpts: Hazards, First Aid & Safety: The angle of view is the amount of a scene that a lens can take in (p. 33).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 2: Some point and-shoot cameras have a fixed focal length lens, giving you only one angle of view (p. 33).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 3: This angle of view is much like what human eyes see in normal vision, roughly equivalent to a 50mmlens (p. 33).
Hazards, First Aid & Safety Principle 4: Other cameras have zoom lenses, which give a varied focal length and varied angle of view (p. 33).
step_by_step_procedure: Step 1 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Generally, a wide-angle lens will give a larger angle of view, while a telephoto lens compresses the subject and gives a smaller angle of view (p. 33).
Step 2 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): A wide-angle lens is a good choice when you are close to your subject (p. 33).
Step 3 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): A telephoto lens is best for subjects when you can't get up close (p. 33).
Step 4 (Hazards, First Aid & Safety): Earlier we discussed the importance of f-stops in controlling your depth of field and what is in focus (p. 33).

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: While composing photographs outdoors near a canyon rim, roadway, or approaching thunderstorm, what safety rule takes priority over capturing the shot?
quiz_item.question: While composing photographs outdoors near a canyon rim, roadway, or approaching thunderstorm, what safety rule takes priority over capturing the shot?
options: A. Maintain situational awareness of your footing and surroundings before stepping while looking through the viewfinder, and seek shelter immediately if lightning or severe weather approaches.
B. Walk backward while looking continuously through the viewfinder to frame a wider angle near ledges or moving traffic.
C. Hold a carbon-fiber tripod high overhead in an open field during a thunderstorm to keep the camera dry.
D. Climb over safety guardrails at scenic overlooks so foreground fences do not appear in the frame.

quiz_item.correct_answer: A. Maintain situational awareness of your footing and surroundings before stepping while looking through the viewfinder, and seek shelter immediately if lightning or severe weather approaches.
quiz_item.explanation: Correct Answer (A): Photographers frequently get injured when stepping backward or sideways while focused on a viewfinder or LCD screen; always check footing and surroundings before moving, and never use tripods as lightning rods in storms.
